A.text: Continued root development and apexogenesis are listed as successful outcomes of vital pulp therapy in immature roots.

cites.section: Indications and Objectives › Immature permanent teeth

B.text: Successful outcomes include continued root development, so cessation of root development is not a success.

cites.section: Indications and Objectives › Immature permanent teeth

C.text: Apexogenesis requires a vital pulp, so replacing it with nonvital tissue is not a successful outcome.

D.text: Preserving the pulp is of utmost importance to allow apex formation, so eliminating it contradicts the treatment objective.

explanation.text: In teeth with immature roots, successful vital pulp therapy leads to continued root development and apexogenesis.

cites.section: Indications and Objectives › Immature permanent teeth

explanation.text: This depends on keeping the pulp vital and preserved.
